title: Persist the new Journal and content-addressed payloads across restart
goal: Make the new implementation’s decisions, task state and referenced content durable and reconstructable without importing prior-iteration history.
scope: Create a concrete durable Journal adapter and content-addressed store for event payloads, effective policy parameters and later snapshots/output. Embedded SQLite is the proposed local implementation choice; all runtime dependencies remain explicit and repository-contained.

Implement atomic ordered append with expected revision, coherent read/replay, versioned payload encoding, digest validation and restart. Resolve acknowledged/failed/indeterminate commits without duplicate events; reject corruption, unsupported format and missing content rather than silently repair authoritative history.

Define durable content write/reference ordering, interrupted-write handling and bounded reading. Parameter digests must resolve to actual immutable values; W1-0005/0008 will store exact snapshot/result content through this contract.

Document the durability assumptions of the chosen local filesystem/database. Compatibility preserves events written by this new implementation as features evolve; there is no migration requirement from previous products or old source artifacts.
context: Authority: approved model sections 0/2/4/5.8/9, D-1–D-5 and R-1/R-17/R-19/R-20; greenfield baseline 0c61ff1.

Proposed new crate: crates/ymp-storage with src/{lib,journal,content}.rs and focused storage integration tests. W1-0001 owns Journal/Envelope/MemoryJournal/type boundaries; W1-0002 and later features supply their concrete payloads through the same contract. Add storage dependencies only for this implemented capability.
This task owns durable transaction/content behavior; later features own their payload schemas and use the same Journal contract. No prior SQLite implementation, API, migration or fixture is assumed.
acceptance: A real temporary durable store persists the W1-0001 decision events and effective parameters; reopening yields the same projection/digests and exact content as MemoryJournal through the same kernel consumer. Later feature payloads, starting with W1-0002 intake, use this contract without changing it.

Competing/stale appends, interrupted/indeterminate commits and missing/corrupt/unsupported content preserve atomic history or give a precise refusal. Retrying a known committed append cannot duplicate events.

Restart preserves original effective parameter values after later configuration changes. The implementation documents what its actual durability test establishes, without claiming prior-iteration compatibility or inaccessible native effects.
